stories.headline: Broncos' Sean Payton: J.K. Dobbins suspended one game for detrimental conduct
stories.summary: The Broncos have suspended running back J.K. Dobbins for one game for conduct detrimental to the team.
stories.body:
The Denver Broncos have suspended running back J.K. Dobbins for one game for conduct detrimental to the team, coach Sean Payton said Tuesday.

Payton did not provide further details.

Dobbins, who has been surpassed as the starter on the Broncos' depth chart by rookie Jonah Coleman, had just one carry in Sunday's 38-24 victory over the visiting Las Vegas Raiders. Coleman starred in the game, rushing for 111 yards and scoring three touchdowns.

Dobbins will miss Friday's road game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Dobbins, 27, re-signed with the Broncos on a two-year, $16 million contract in March. Last season, his first with Denver, he led the team with 772 yards rushing and also had four rushing touchdowns.

This season, he has 324 yards rushing -- which still leads the team -- and three rushing touchdowns.

stories.headline: Champions League recap: Dortmund snatch point at Arsenal, Madrid go top
stories.summary: Borussia Dortmund earned a crucial point away at Arsenal, while Real Madrid got an easy win over PSV on the first day of Matchday 5 of the UEFA Champions League.
stories.body:
The Champions!

The UEFA Champions League returned Tuesday for Matchday 5 of the league phase, with nine matches across the continent as the race for a place in the knockout rounds continued to heat up!

One of our main matches of the day had reigning Premier League champions -- and current league leaders -- Arsenal play out a 1-1 draw with Bundesliga leaders Borussia Dortmund.

Elsewhere, Manchester City were held to a 2-2 draw by Napoli, while Real Madrid cruised to a 5-1 win over PSV Eindhoven.

In the early kickoffs, Bodø/Glimt edged LASK 1-0, while Aston Villa suffered a 1-0 defeat to Galatasaray in Istanbul.

In the remaining matches, Como beat AEK Athens 1-0, FC Porto secured a 1-0 win over Feyenoord, RB Leipzig overcame Lens 3-1 and Real Betis defeated Slovan Bratislava 2-0.

Enjoy all that happened from Tuesday's matches across Europe!

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Arsenal, Newcastle eye Inter's Pio Esposito
stories.summary: Both Arsenal and Newcastle United are looking to improve their attack by signing Inter's Pio Esposito. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Arsenal and Newcastle United are competing to sign Internazionale striker Pio Esposito, while Bayern Munich's Luis Díaz and Chelsea's Estêvão are on the shortlist of UEFA Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Arsenal and Newcastle United are monitoring Internazionale striker Pio Esposito, according to Nicolo Schira. The Serie A club are reporrted to have turned down approaches worth around €60 million for the 21-year-old, who is contracted until 2032, and viewed as an indispensable member of manager Cristian Chivu's squad. Esposito scored a hat trick in the 4-4 league draw with Atalanta on Sunday and was also on target in both of Italy's Nations League clashes this month, as he scored a brace in the 3-1 win over France on Nov. 12.

- Paris Saint-Germain have added Bayern Munich's Luis Díaz and Chelsea's Estêvão to their shortlist, as they consider whether to strengthen their forward line following the long-term injuries sustained by Désiré Doué and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, according to Diario AS. PSG manager Luis Enrique wants to take time before making a decision, amid plans to assess the squad in the coming weeks, but the club have identified the 29-year-old Díaz as an option due to his direct dribbling style and Estêvão, 19, is also on the Ligue 1 club's radar due to his limited minutes in London.

- Chelsea are keeping tabs on Tottenham Hotspur winger Luca Williams-Barnett, who is closing in on signing a new contract, the Daily Telegraph reports. The Blues are watching the 18-year-old's situation alongside Borussia Dortmund, but Spurs are reportedly now handling the final details on an extension which could ward off interest in his signature. Williams-Barnett registered a goal and an assist on his first Premier League start in the 2-0 win over Ipswich Town on Saturday.

- Manchester United are preparing an approach for United States and Villarreal right back Alex Freeman, Football Insider reports. Scouts are reported to have been impressed by the 22-year-old's performances on multiple occasions, and the Red Devils have made him one of their top priorities for January in a move that would see him reunite with former USMNT manager Mauricio Pochettino. Freeman has made 16 appearances for the Yellow Submarine this season, continuing form since impressing at the 2026 World Cup in the summer.

- Bayern Munich are considering an approach for New York Red Bulls striker Eric Maxim Choupo-Moting, Sky Germany reports. The Bundesliga club are keen to acquire a short-term replacement for Harry Kane, who is set to be sidelined for several months following a ligament tear. Choupo-Moting, 37, is expected to be available as a free agent at the end of the year when his contract expires in Major League Soccer, and he is seen as a strong option due to his familiarity with the club. He directly contributed to 51 goals in 122 matches during a four-year spell at the Allianz Arena which ended in 2024.

Other
- Manchester United are interested in Brentford defender Nathan Collins as a potential alternative to Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite, whose transfer would require an offer worth in excess of £70 million. (Daily Mail)

- Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham is in advanced talks regarding a new contract. (Athletic)

- Liverpool have begun contract talks with 34-year-old goalkeeper Alisson. (Nicolo Schira)

- Manchester United are keen to sign a striker in January. (Times)

- Bayern Munich aren't currently exploring a move for Real Madrid right back Trent Alexander-Arnold despite reports. (Christian Falk)

- Manchester United and Chelsea are weighing up approaches for Napoli midfielder Scott McTominay. (Il Mattino)

- Liverpool and Brighton are battling to sign Borussia Monchengladbach attacking midfielder Wael Mohya. (TEAMtalk)

- Como are monitoring the situation of Manchester United striker Joshua Zirkzee. (Nicolo Schira)

- Atletico Madrid and Juventus are planning to send scouts to watch Sporting CP left back Maxi Araujo during the Champions League match against Manchester United on Wednesday. (Record)

- Chelsea are tracking Bayern Munich goalkeeper Leonard Prescott. (Christian Falk)

- Juventus, Newcastle, Brentford and Bournemouth are interested in Lazio midfielder Kenneth Taylor. (TEAMtalk)

stories.headline: Fantasy baseball reactions to MLB offseason trades, signings
stories.summary: Track all the latest MLB free agency and trade news with fantasy baseball analysis from Tristan H. Cockcroft and Eric Karabell.
stories.byline: Tristan H. Cockcroft and Eric Karabell
stories.body:
Tracking the offseason MLB trades and signings with fantasy baseball implications for the upcoming season, Eric Karabell and Tristan H. Cockcroft will analyze and provide an outlook for all of the key players involved.

Players were allowed to sign with new teams beginning Nov. 2, although typically things don't really start to heat up until the league's annual winter meetings. This year's meetings are scheduled to take place in San Diego from Dec. 7-9. However, with the current collective bargaining agreement expiring Dec. 1, players and teams alike might end up waiting until after the dust settles on negotiations and a potential lockout before inking any new deals.

In any event, as any contracts are signed or trades get agreed to, this is the place to find all of the fantasy fallout of those deals. Be sure to check back throughout the hot stove season for updates. Latest updates include the Toronto Blue Jays signing Japanese star Kaima Taira, the Chicago Cubs signing both Trevor Rogers and Teroaki Sato and Freddy Peralta signing with the Baltimore Orioles.

Below, you will find a list of some of the top free agents at each position. Players labeled with a (Q) received a qualifying offer from their current team and had until Nov. 17 to accept it or decline and become a free agent. Players coming from Japan/Korea who were posted by their current team have a Dec. 1 deadline to reach a deal with an MLB club to play in the United States in 2027.

Note: Not every transaction warrants the attention of fantasy managers, but for those signings and trades that do merit analysis, you'll find them listed below. Players will be separated by position and then listed in chronological order of the move within each positional grouping, with the latest news coming first. Also included are links to any standalone analysis stories and/or videos regarding major free agent signings and trades. Players who end up re-signing with their previous team will not always be included.

Jump to:

Catcher | First base | Second base | Shortstop | Third base

Outfield | DH | Starting pitcher | Relief pitcher

Catcher
Some free agents: Carson Kelly, Tyler Stephenson, Kyle Higashioka, Gary Sanchez, James McCann, Travis d'Arnaud, Austin Hedges

First base
Paul Goldschmidt signs with Mets
Goldschmidt, 39, hit only .252 over 380 PA with the Yankees last season -- but how he did so explains why the Mets coveted him. Goldschmidt hit .299/.393/.573 with 11 home runs versus left-handed pitching, one year after posting a .336/.411/.570 line. He has not enjoyed recent success against right-handed pitching. The Mets figure to platoon Goldschmidt, perhaps with lefty-hitting Jared Young. While that should be productive for the team, it isn't so great for fantasy managers.

Goldschmidt finished outside the top 50 first basemen in 2026 scoring. Roster him in daily formats, when you can take advantage of knowing exactly when he will be in the lineup. Fade him in standard leagues. -- Karabell (11/23)

Jake Bauers signs with Red Sox
Bauers, 31, comes off the best season of his journeyman career, posting an .873 OPS with 26 homers and 86 RBIs for the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers. He admits that he considered retirement as recently as two years ago, but he stuck around for the health benefits. Good timing. Bauers gets a four-year deal with the Red Sox, where he and right-handed-hitting Willson Contreras should make for a formidable 1-2 punch in the middle of the lineup, while sharing 1B/DH duties.

While Bauers was a top-40 hitter in points formats and roto/categories leagues last season, fantasy managers probably shouldn't expect the same kind of production moving forward, even as he performs half the time at hitter-friendly Fenway Park. Bauers had never hit more than 12 home runs in any prior season and, even now, he remains a career .223 hitter with a 2.0 career WAR.

Maybe the solid 16.3% walk rate and .218 ISO will continue, but preliminary results in NFBC drafts have Bauers going just inside the top 150. Perhaps he gets a bump for heading to Boston, but likely only a modest one. -- Karabell (11/13)

Other free agents: Josh Bell, Ryan Mountcastle, Nathaniel Lowe, Ty France

Second base

Some free agents: Gleyber Torres, Jeff McNeil, Luis Arraez, Jazz Chisholm Jr., Jonathan India, Gavin Lux, Brandon Lowe (Q)

Shortstop

Some free agents: Ha-Seong Kim, J.P. Crawford, Mauricio Dubon, Isiah Kiner-Falefa, Amed Rosario

Third base
Teruaki Sato signs with Cubs
Sato, 27 and the defending Nippon Central League Triple Crown winner, reminds many of another left-handed hitting Japanese slugger who came to the United States. Chicago White Sox 1B Munetaka Murakami, who, in his first MLB season, launched 35 home runs with a 16.6% walk rate, albeit with a .207 batting average and 35.4% strikeout rate. Sato is viewed as a better athlete, but expected to offer a similar offensive profile in the "three true outcomes" department, with power, walks and strikeouts.

This profile has value in fantasy, but Murakami averaged only 2.1 ESPN fantasy points per game, outside the top 100 hitters. He was the No. 127 hitter on the Player Rater, even though only nine hitters slugged more home runs. Should potential Sato investors expect better numbers than Murakami's debut? Sato may boast better plate discipline and a better likelihood to adjust his approach, perhaps trading some power for better contact. Fangraphs projects a .247 batting average and 30 home runs. While Murakami is not among ESPN's initial top 200 for points formats, Sato should earn a better ranking, though not among the top 100.

Though Sato is likely ticketed for an outfield corner with the Cubs, he will be eligible at third base only in fantasy drafts based on his games played in Japan in 2026. He can earn additional eligibility with 10 games played at another position in 2027. -- Karabell (11/24)

Royce Lewis traded to Dodgers
Lewis, 27 and a former first-round pick of the Twins in 2017, has long been ticketed for slugging stardom, but his road to becoming one of the premier, power-hitting third basemen has been bumpy. Lewis hit 15 home runs and knocked in 52 over 58 games and 239 PA during his breakout 2023 campaign, with a .920 OPS. Injuries have derailed him since, as Lewis has neither reached 20 home runs in a season nor approached a .800 OPS.

At least Lewis managed to stay healthy enough to reach 500 PA for the first time in 2026, though he struck out in 25.5% of his PA with a career-low 71.9% contact rate. Can the Los Angeles Dodgers get him consistently productive and keep him on the field? The Minnesota Twins clearly could not. Eligible at first base and third base, perhaps the Dodgers view Lewis as a utility option and lefty killer, but if he doesn't hit, it doesn't matter. Bump Lewis up your draft sheets a bit because of this trade, but he remains more of a late-round sleeper than a sure thing. -- Karabell 11/20

Maikel Garcia traded to Mariners
Garcia, 26, suffered through a rough 2026 season, missing months with hamstring and hand injuries, and slugging only .381 during his 82 games and 344 PA. Not that Garcia is a renowned power hitter, but he delivered 16 home runs among his 60 extra-base hits in a breakout 2025, along with 23 stolen bases, after stealing 37 bases in 2024. Garcia missed only seven games during 2024-25, so volume played a role when he finished 18th among hitters in 2025 fantasy points.

A 2025 Gold Glove winner, Garcia is one of the better defensive third basemen in baseball, and he should solidify the position for Seattle. However, while we don't know for sure where he will hit in his new lineup -- and leaving one hitter-challenging home ballpark in Kansas City for another does not help him -- it figures to be near the bottom half, which caps his fantasy upside. Expect Garcia to bounce back to some degree offensively, with his early ESPN 2027 points ranking featuring him positively as the No. 10 3B and just outside the top 100. -- Karabell (11/18)

Some free agents: Alec Bohm, Eugenio Suarez, Edmundo Sosa, Yoan Moncada, Si Hwan Roh (posted)

Outfield

Some free agents: George Springer, Trent Grisham, Ian Happ, Seiya Suzuki (Q), Randy Arozarena, Taylor Ward, Daulton Varsho, Adolis Garcia, Luis Robert Jr., Randal Grichuk, Myles Straw, Lane Thomas

Designated hitter

Some free agents: Joc Pederson, Dominic Smith

Starting pitcher
Tarik Skubal signs with Mets
Two winters ago, the New York Mets opened their wallet to get their offensive centerpiece, Juan Soto. On Sunday, the Mets did the same to get a centerpiece for their rotation, and for a similarly record-setting deal, signing Tarik Skubal to a nine-year, $450 million contract.

Fortunately for us in fantasy, we won't need to spend as much as the Mets did to add Skubal to our rosters, but it's a good landing spot for the lefty. He'll call one of the more pitching-leaning ballparks in Citi Field his home through 2036. -- Cockcroft (11/23)

For a more in-depth look at the fantasy impact of Skubal's signing, click here.

Toronto Blue Jays sign SP Kaima Taira

Having missed out on their top free-agent pitching prize, Tarik Skubal, the Blue Jays moved quickly to sign Taira, who by many accounts had the second-best raw stuff of any pitcher on this winter's market, to a five-year, $80 million contract. Taira spent seven of his first eight seasons in Japan as a reliever but transitioned beautifully to a starting pitching role in 2026, posting a Nippon Professional Baseball-leading 1.36 ERA across 22 starts and one relief appearance. Prior to that, he had posted sub-2 ERAs in each of his prior five seasons working out of the bullpen (2020-22, '24-25), 31 saves in 2025, as well as a 2.40 ERA in 23 starts while pitching out of the rotation in 2023.

That's a remarkable level of success for a pitcher who stands just 5-foot-8. Marcus Stroman is the only MLB pitcher this century who stood that height or shorter to have made as many as 10 starts. Taira's extension -- measuring the distance from the pitching rubber that the pitcher releases the baseball -- is regarded as elite, however, and to a point where he'd likely rank in the upper quarter in U.S. play in that department. Between that and his six -- and, by some accounts, as many as eight -- pitches in his repertoire, he counters the height question with a great deal of upside. Taira's command of his pitch mix is considered elite, and generally ground ball-generating, so even with some anticipated regression to his strikeout rate he might well deliver numbers that place among the top 40 pitchers in fantasy baseball.

We'll see how swiftly and smoothly Taira adapts to U.S. play, which despite becoming less demanding upon starting pitchers in the post-COVID era, still has a lengthier and more physically taxing schedule. Questions about whether he's more suited for relief than rotation work are valid, and the primary obstacle towards him earning that potential top-40 starter ranking. By signing in Toronto, where he's more likely to have the team's patience with his adapting to the rotation, Saito will earn a ranking around No. 75 at the position, in the Joey Cantillo/Trey Yesavage/Eduardo Rodriguez range. -- Cockcroft (11/24)

RHP Freddy Peralta signs with Orioles

Peralta, 30, ended the 2026 season with a bloated 4.42 ERA and 1.33 WHIP, but those numbers hardly tell the story. The longtime Brewers ace who struck out 200 hitters during three consecutive seasons started the 2026 season with the Mets after an offseason trade, and things went poorly right away. Then, months later, the Mets traded Peralta to the Rays and, voila, all was well again!

With his mechanics tweaked and his approach refined (more changeups, fewer sliders), Peralta posted a 3.25 ERA and 1.01 WHIP during 10 Rays starts, albeit with a lower strikeout rate than typical, but at least he was good. Then he thrived in the postseason, winning ALCS MVP honors. That is what fantasy managers expect. Peralta may not be a top 20 starting pitcher for fantasy, but he should be close. Peralta ranks among the top 100 players for points and roto formats. -- Karabell (11/24)

LHP Trevor Rogers signs with Cubs
Rogers, 29, was never going to match his incredible 2025 season, when he posted a 1.81 ERA and 0.90 WHIP during 18 starts, but his 2026 campaign (4.03, 1.18) may have still exceeded some expectations. After all, the 6-foot-5 left-hander posted a 4.92 ERA and 1.58 WHIP for the Marlins and Orioles in 2024. The 2017 first-round pick dealt with injuries, control issues and inconsistency for much of his career, among other things. Then, suddenly, he was a star, even for half a season.

Rogers probably isn't a star. The Cubs get a guy who made 30 starts (for the first time) and did his best work in the second half, with a 3.52 ERA and 1.04 WHIP, whiffing 27% of hitters. That's good, reliable work, and Rogers was among the top 40 starting pitchers in ESPN fantasy points. Can the Cubs and fantasy managers get that version in 2027? That seems reasonable. Rogers isn't an ace, but worthy of being among the top 40 starters in drafts. There is nothing wrong with that. --Karabell (11/24)

Luis Castillo and Davis Martin traded to Rockies
What happens when the league's worst non-Rockies or Athletics pitcher (minimum 130 innings) comes to Coors Field? We're about to find out. Castillo entered 2026 riding a four-year streak with at least 350 fantasy points, 160 strikeouts and a sub-1.20 WHIP. However, a progressive drop in his velocity and a rise in his fly ball rate during that time caused him to unravel last year, first for the Seattle Mariners and then catastrophically so following his midseason trade to the Chicago White Sox. Castillo's year ended with a shoulder injury, so in addition to the Coors factor, he enters 2027 facing many questions.

Martin, meanwhile, was the far superior fantasy pitcher between these two -- by almost two times in terms of point production (242-127). Martin, though, ended 2026 on a similarly sour note. He had a 9-2 record and 2.41 ERA through his first 13 starts, but went 0-8 with a 5.72 ERA thereafter. He dealt with a calf issue, a blister and concerns that he might be tipping pitches, ultimately making only a mop-up appearance during Chicago's playoff run.

Martin was nevertheless the piece the Rockies wanted in order to agree to absorb Castillo's remaining contract. Both will probably eat innings for a Rockies rotation always in need of depth. Either could be a "matchup candidate" in road games, if they seem to have righted the ship during spring training -- which is why a lockout-influenced, shortened preseason would be detrimental to both. Still, neither pitcher is a draft-day option, given their new team. -- Cockcroft (11/20)

Twins sign SP Sonny Gray
Gray, now 37 years old, returns to Minnesota after a three-year detour through St. Louis and Boston. He has enjoyed a bit of a career rebirth later in his career, averaging 385.8 fantasy points over the past four seasons, and never deviating by more than 25 points in either direction in any individual year. Gray's consistency is a valuable thing in fantasy leagues, particularly points-based scoring, where his good ratios and solid innings totals are most advantageous.

That said, a two-year pattern of declining average fastball velocity and strikeout rates raises concerns that regression might hit him harder than a typical frontline starter, if not in 2027 then perhaps if he doesn't opt out and continues into his 39-year-old campaign in 2028. I've got Gray ranked amongst my top 25 fantasy starting pitchers, and within the top 75 overall, and I'd expect he will (and should) generally be drafted in that range.

Gray's acquisition, however, gives the Twins at least nine viable rotation candidates, creating a logjam of popular deep-mixed/AL-only names like Mick Abel, Zebby Matthews, Connor Prielipp for fourth/fifth starter spots. Perhaps a trade is forthcoming, preferably for some hitting to bolster the lineup and give Gray more run support, but otherwise this is a spring battle that'll be high on the list of those to watch. Only Gray, Joe Ryan, Taj Bradley and Pablo Lopez would figure to be locks. -- Cockcroft (11/18)

Bryce Miller traded to Royals
Miller, 28, emerged as a standout fantasy option for the Seattle Mariners in 2024, winning 12 games and posting a 2.94 ERA and 0.98 WHIP. Injuries and inconsistency have plagued the right-hander since then, as Miller won only eight of 39 starts in 2025-26 with a 4.82 ERA and 1.26 WHIP while permitting 38 home runs. Elbow woes ruined his 2025 campaign, and he missed the first six weeks of 2026 with an oblique injury.

Still, when Miller is healthy, he can be effective. He posted a 2.18 ERA and 0.83 WHIP prior to the 2026 All-Star break before a rough second half (and myriad home runs) ruined things. Moving from one pitcher's park in Seattle to another in Kansas City shouldn't be a factor, but at least Miller should be guaranteed a rotation spot, which was in question in Seattle. Miller is certainly a sleeper candidate to regain his place among the top 30 starting pitchers in fantasy, but ESPN's preliminary points ranking features Miller well outside the top 50 starting pitchers. -- Karabell (11/18)

Dustin May signs with White Sox
May, 29, made 31 mostly league-average starts for the Cardinals and eventual champion Brewers this season -- many of them quite abbreviated. In fact, he ended up averaging fewer than four innings over his 10 Brewers starts and he did not qualify for the ERA title. The desperate White Sox figure to allow May to go deeper into games, but that comes at a cost, since he posted a 4.70 ERA and a 1.32 WHIP with only 0.4 bWAR last season.

Hey, at least May stayed healthy, which is a feat for him. Plus, he was a bit unlucky, as his 3.54 FIP indicates. However, that doesn't mean May warrants inclusion in ESPN standard drafts, with a preliminary points-league rank outside the top 75 starting pitchers. -- Karabell (11/18)

Other free agents: Michael King, Robbie Ray, Brandon Woodruff, Zac Gallen, Shota Imanaga, Kevin Gausman, Chris Bassitt, Jack Flaherty, Jameson Taillon, Max Scherzer, Clay Holmes, Matthew Boyd, Nick Pivetta, Shane Bieber, Nick Martinez, Tyler Mahle, Foster Griffin, Michael Soroka

Relief pitcher
RHP Emilio Pagan signs with Tigers
Pagan, 35, saved 57 games for the Cincinnati Reds over the past two seasons, although his 2025 numbers were rather ordinary (3.38 ERA, 25.9% K rate). Still, this is a franchise that desired Kenley Jansen and let him save 22 games last season even though there were better pitchers in the bullpen. Pagan produced nearly identical stats to Jansen. In other words, Pagan isn't so valuable -- but if all you care about are saves in a roto format, a healthy Pagan should provide at least 25 of them. -- Karabell (11/13)

RHP Evan Phillips signs with Braves
Phillips, 32, posted a 2.36 ERA over parts of six seasons for the Los Angeles Dodgers. He also accrued 42 combined saves during 2023 and 2024. He missed most of 2025 dealing with Tommy John surgery and returned last season to pitch 26 effective innings. Additionally, Phillips has never permitted a run over 18⅓ postseason innings. The Braves figure to turn to RHP Robert Suarez to close (because Raisel Iglesias is a free agent), but a healthy Phillips should accrue ample holds as well as occasional saves. -- Karabell (11/13)

Other free agents: Raisel Iglesias, Pete Fairbanks, Carlos Estevez, A.J. Minter, Blake Treinen, Martin Perez, Gregory Soto, Kenley Jansen, Hiromi Itoh (posted)

stories.headline: WNBA players elect Elizabeth Williams as union president
stories.summary: Sky center Elizabeth Williams was elected president of the Women's National Basketball Players Association and will replace Nneka Ogwumike, who had been in the role since 2016.
stories.body:
Chicago Sky center Elizabeth Williams was elected president of the Women's National Basketball Players Association and will replace Nneka Ogwumike, who retired after being in the role since 2016.

Williams, who will serve out the final two years of Ogwumike's term that began earlier this year, was picked by players on Tuesday over Breanna Stewart of the New York Liberty and Gabby Williams of the Golden State Valkyries, a source with knowledge of the ballot told ESPN.

A 12-year veteran, Williams joined the WNBPA executive committee in 2018 and served four two-year terms. She has been at the bargaining table for two CBAs, including the most recent agreement that raised maximum player salaries to over $1 million.

"One of my main goals as president is to increase the engagement of the younger members of this union," Williams said in a statement to WNBPA player representatives. "I know the value of diverse voices in these conversations. We may not always agree, but I want to make sure every player knows that her voice is being heard.

"This is the strength of our union. I am grateful for what we have accomplished over these last few years, and I'm excited about the potential for a new opportunity to serve."

The WNBA will also have a new face leading the league office as commissioner Cathy Engelbert is retiring at the end of the year. A search for her replacement is ongoing.

Williams will lead the executive committee comprised of Napheesa Collier (1st vice president), Veronica Burton (secretary), Chelsea Gray (treasurer), and three additional vice presidents: Alysha Clark, Ezi Magbegor, and Maya Caldwell.

Burton, Gray, Magbegor and Caldwell join the executive committee for the first time.

"These election results reflect the strength of our union and the power of player leadership," WNBPA executive director Terri Carmichael Jackson said in a statement. "Congratulations to Elizabeth and each of our newly elected and returning Executive Committee members, whose collective experience, diverse perspectives, and commitment will help guide the WNBPA into its next chapter.

"As we turn our focus to implementing our transformational CBA and building on the progress our members have fought so hard to achieve, our greatest strength remains our unity, our democratic process, and our unwavering commitment to one another."

Williams, who was selected fourth overall in the 2015 WNBA draft out of Duke and was the 2016 Most Improved Player, becomes president after a lengthy period of stability in union leadership.

Ogwumike, the outgoing WNBPA president, announced her WNBA retirement during the 2026 season. An 11-time All-Star and the 2016 MVP, Ogwumike has served as WNBPA president since 2016, presiding over two collective bargaining agreement negotiations and shaping the social justice activism that defined the player body during her tenure.

stories.headline: Fantasy notebook: Karabell on Paul George, Tyler Herro, De'Aaron Fox, more
stories.summary: Eric Karabell empties out the notebook with all that he's noticing around the NBA and what it means for fantasy.
stories.body:
When the Boston Celtics stunningly traded star SF/SG Jaylen Brown to the rival Philadelphia 76ers this past summer, Celtics fans groaned not only about losing a key 10-year veteran who averaged 28.7 PPG last season, but about the once-great SF/PF Paul George joining the roster as his replacement. Meanwhile, 76ers fans mightily celebrated George leaving it.

Was all that fair? Probably not, especially in retrospect, because we are in the seventh week of the NBA season with Brown and George performing at a similar statistical level, with George well ahead on the Player Rater (No. 42 to No. 75) and averaging 39.5 ESPN fantasy points per game, just a bit ahead of Brown at 38.5 points. Who would have expected this development?

Let's focus not on Brown, who is doing precisely what the 76ers expected him to do in a star-filled lineup, averaging 22.4 PPG in 34.3 MPG, but on George, who has been a solid fit for Boston's aggressive 3-point field goal attack. George, 36 and averaging 19.9 PPG in 30.1 MPG, rested for Sunday night's road game versus the Golden State Warriors (which the Celtics lost!), but this tragic figure, who participated in only 78 of a possible 164 games during two disappointing 76ers seasons, has missed only three games this season -- just like Brown.

Durability was likely the biggest concern for fantasy managers potentially interested in George, which is why he fell to Round 7, at least, in ESPN average live drafts. Most fantasy managers probably looked at Brown's lofty numbers from last season (achieved sans injured teammate Jayson Tatum) and could not wait to invest among the first 30 selections. Still, one could see a path to similar production if the games were similar . We can check back on comparing these fellows in a month and, who knows, perhaps George is hurt again tomorrow, and the entire premise was silly. Then again, perhaps not.

The Celtics keep George's minutes in check, and more than half his attempted field goals are from 3-point range. He's hitting 40.7% on 3-pointers. George is also fourth in the NBA in steals per game, such a critical differentiator in roto formats. His three missed games each came during the second half of back-to-back outings, and we should expect that continues. That's fine, really, hardly atypical behavior for veterans in this league. If it keeps George healthy for 65 games, a figure he has reached in one of the past seven seasons, we are all for it. Give George credit. He was caught in an awkward situation, but these numbers are solid.

Ultimately, even though production and health are similar today, it is hard to make a great case to trade Brown for George in a points format or a roto/categories league, but it isn't nearly as wild a thought as it was when this real-life trade occurred, or even two months ago. One of these fellows is, predictably, not earning great value from his fantasy draft-day status. The other has been, well, a steal.

Other observations around the NBA

Three players scored 50 traditional points during the past week. Nobody should be surprised when San Antonio Spurs unicorn C Victor Wembanyama does it. (He scored 116 fantasy points in that game versus the New Orleans Pelicans!) Perhaps there was some surprise when Cleveland Cavaliers PG/SG James Harden, averaging 18.4 PPG for the season, dropped 51 points on the Indiana Pacers (80 fantasy points). I wrote about Harden recently, expecting his performance to improve but notably for assists. It has, and there is little indication the 51-point game is anything but an outlier.
Then Milwaukee Bucks SG/PG Tyler Herro scored 50 points (89 fantasy points) in a close, tough loss to the 76ers Saturday, as a game-tying 3-pointer at the buzzer was deemed a split second late. Herro torched Philly that afternoon, but it was only the second time all season he had even reached 30 points in any game. (He scored 32 points on Monday.) Herro is averaging a team-leading 21.9 PPG, the only Bucks player at more than 15 PPG, and we did reasonably expect more from him on a team bereft of proven talent. Shouldn't Herro be scoring 25-27 PPG? Perhaps he will, but I'm not sure I would trade for him expecting it. Herro is playing 31 MPG, and he has missed half the season in two of three years. Be realistic, even though the Bucks lack their first-round pick next season. The Bucks may not push him to 65-plus games.
Is Warriors C Charles Bassey this week's version of Utah Jazz C Mo Bamba? I wrote about Bamba last week, noting his unlikely 26-point explosion on Nov. 15 (6-6 on 3-pointers!) was fun, and many were adding him, but c'mon, he's not that good. Bamba then delivered three double-digit rebound outings last week, so I kept him around. Bassey, 26 and with his fourth NBA franchise, averaged 13 PPG and 10 RPG during three starts last week. The Warriors are desperate, and they stopped a five-game losing streak against the Celtics Sunday night. Good for Bassey, but I think I would stick with Bamba, if I were to stick with either one. C Kristaps Porzingis, his NBA career perhaps over, remains rostered in 31% of ESPN leagues. We are way past the point that managers must move on.
I lack shares of Sacramento Kings rookie PG Darius Acuff Jr., but I can't stop eagerly watching his box scores. First, how is this fellow not the obvious choice for Rookie of the Year? He's averaging 24.6 PPG and 7.2 APG in a wild 36.6 MPG. Several other top rookies are hurt and only Denver Nuggets Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray are averaging more minutes. Acuff is hitting only 40.3% on field goals, which is somewhat a problem for fantasy investors, but not really much of any detriment in the big picture, but we cannot help but notice his past three games: only 17 PPG (against better defensive teams) and 33% on field goals (20-for-60). Should fantasy investors look to move this rookie for safer, veteran talent? Harden, LaMelo Ball and Darius Garland are point guards with fewer fantasy points. Yeah, I would take them. This is a ton of minutes for a fellow who played in all of 36 college games at Arkansas (one season), though he averaged 35.1 MPG. The Kings are 2-15. Do you think Acuff is playing through a rolled ankle for a seven-win team in February? Me neither.
You know how you manage several fantasy hoops teams and sometimes you just leave a star active because you either don't have a suitable replacement or you don't realize just how badly he was playing? That's where I am with Spurs PG/SG De'Aaron Fox. OK, I knew he was underachieving, but 12.4 PPG? He averaged 26.6 PPG only three seasons ago, and 18.6 PPG last year with the Spurs. What changed? Oh, PG/SG Dylan Harper is simply a better player, and these two have swapped volume. Fox has gone from 14.5 field goal attempts to 8.5, which is stunning. Harper (hip) is hurt and Fox, who missed Monday's game with a shin contusion, has gotten worse, scoring only 21 points over the past three games in 92 minutes. No, we cannot drop Fox, for the 5.8 APG and solid shooting soothe us some, but 119 players average more than 12.4 PPG, including Nolan Traore, Jonathan Kuminga and Terrence Shannon Jr. This is awful.

stories.headline: Lightning forward Conor Geekie out 4-5 months after undergoing shoulder surgery

stories.body:
Tampa Bay Lightning forward Conor Geekie is expected to miss the next four to five months after undergoing shoulder surgery, the team said Tuesday.

Geekie skated 14 shifts for more than eight minutes of ice time on Nov. 14 against Detroit and finished that game but has missed the past two. He had surgery Monday, the team said. The 22-year-old has four goals and one assist this season.

The Lightning acquired Geekie from Utah at the 2024 draft as part of the return for two-time Stanley Cup-winning defenseman Mikhail Sergachev.

stories.headline: Fiona the hippo to be honored by FC Cincinnati with tifo after untimely death
stories.summary: FC Cincinnati will honor Cincinnati Zoo's famous hippo, Fiona, following her unexpected death last week.
stories.body:
FC Cincinnati will honor Fiona, the local hippo who became famous on social media, following her unexpected death last week.

The MLS side is planning to unveil a special tifo to pay tribute to Fiona prior to their MLS Cup playoff match against Nashville on Saturday.

Fiona was beloved by many in Cincinnati, Ohio, and around the world. Fiona died of health complications last Thursday following after she swallowed a child's knit cap that had landed in her enclosure at Cincinnati Zoo.

The Nile hippopotamus became a worldwide sensation when she was born in 2017 at the zoo. Fiona arrived six weeks premature and her chances of survival were low.

But she beat the odds to make it through and grew into a viral star.

In 2017, local ice cream chain Graeter's even released a limited-edition flavor inspired by Fiona. It was called "Chunky Chunky Hippo."

FC Cincinnati said Fiona "became a symbol of Cincinnati and captured hearts around the world."

During FC Cincinnati's 3-1 win over Orlando on the day of Fiona's death, defender Nick Hagglund dedicated his goal to the hippo by exclaiming "that's for Fiona" before mimicking her ears on the top of his head.

Fiona was also honored by other Cincinnati sports teams upon news of her death, including NFL team Cincinnati Bengals and MLB side Cincinnati Reds. They both posted tributes to the much-loved hippo on their social media accounts.

- Bengals, Reds pay tribute to Fiona the hippo after her death

- NFL Week 11 arrivals: Tee Higgins pays homage to Fiona the Hippo ahead of 'MNF'

Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins even wore a Fiona sweater on Monday night before his team lost to the Washington Commanders.

FC Cincinnati will also make a donation for every fan in attendance at TQL Stadium to the Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden in Fiona's memory.

Speaking about Fiona's death, the Cincinnati Zoo director Dave Jenike said: "Our animal care team was heroic in their efforts to save her. They did everything possible, but her body couldn't fight anymore.

"She was dearly loved by her Zoo family and countless others around the world. Her loss will be felt deeply by so many."

FC Cincinnati can progress to the Eastern Conference semifinal with a win over Nashville on Saturday.

Formula 1 heads to Qatar for the second leg of its final triple header of the 2026 season.

Max Verstappen fended off his rivals to take a stunning victory under the lights at the Las Vegas Grand Prix last time out.

McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri took the final spots on the podium.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the 22nd round.

Weather forecast

The weather for the Qatar Grand Prix is forecast to be sunny with a gentle breeze across the weekend. It's a night race so conditions are dry with highs of 24°C on Sunday.

McLaren's Piastri pipped teammate Norris to pole position as the battle for the world title continued with two races remaining.

Piastri was leading the race and Norris was running in third, but the Papaya team decided against pitting under the Safety Car. Piastri ended the race in second, with Norris in fourth.

Who will win this year?

Verstappen looked unstoppable in Las Vegas and will be targeting his fifth win of the season in Qatar.

Mercedes' Russell was well in the mix last time out but will be looking to respond after Verstappen said the Englishman was "so far below his level" as their feud intensified.

Both teams look strong, so the rivalry could well continue in Qatar. Drivers up and down the grid will also be limited to 27 laps on each set of tyres, which will play massively into teams' strategies.

Tensions between Ferrari teammates Hamilton and Charles Leclerc continue to heat up after boss Fred Vasseur labelled them "unmanageable."

Don't count out new world champion Kimi Antonelli who is always one to watch after an impressive season.
